Getting started

Install the Python package

The native library must be built for the platform where the program will run. From the repository root, select a backend and build the project:

$ ./configure.sh
$ make

On Linux, the default backend is XCB. You can select Wayland with make BACKEND=wayland. On macOS, use make BACKEND=appkit. The build script checks the required system packages and tools; see the repository root README.md for backend dependencies and configuration details.

The build creates a wheel in the repository root. Install the generated wheel inside the virtual environment for your application:

$ python -m pip install ./mlx-*-py3-none-any.whl

Then import and initialize the wrapper:

from mlx import Mlx

mlx = Mlx()
mlx_ptr = mlx.mlx_init()
if mlx_ptr is None:
    raise RuntimeError("Could not connect to the display")

mlx_init must succeed before creating windows or images. Mlx() loads the shared library from beside the installed Python module, so the wheel and the native library need to come from the same build.

Build these docs

Install the documentation dependencies and build the HTML site:

$ python -m pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
$ sphinx-build -b html docs docs/_build/html

The HTML entry point is docs/_build/html/index.html. Read the Docs uses the same Sphinx configuration and the Read the Docs theme.

Python wrapper behavior

The wrapper keeps the native function names and generally the same argument order as the C API. Native pointers are represented as integer-like handles; pass them back to MLX methods and do not inspect or modify them. Methods that create a connection, window, or image return None on failure.

Several C functions fill output pointers. Their Python equivalents return the outputs directly:

  • mlx_get_data_addr(img_ptr) returns (pixels, bits_per_pixel, size_line, format). pixels is a writable memoryview.

  • mlx_mouse_get_pos(win_ptr) returns (status, x, y).

  • mlx_get_screen_size(mlx_ptr) returns (status, width, height).

  • mlx_xpm_file_to_image and mlx_png_file_to_image return (image, width, height).

Hook methods accept Python callables and an arbitrary param object. The wrapper retains references to registered callbacks and parameters for as long as they are registered. Pass callback=None to clear a hook.
